draft.title: Representation of people and places
card: A representation is how a text portrays a person, group or place. It is not the real thing. It is a version built by the creator.
Creators choose what to include, what to leave out, and which words, images and viewpoints to use. These choices shape how the audience sees the subject.
Context also shapes a representation. The creator's time, place, values and purpose affect how they portray someone or somewhere.
Two texts can portray the same town differently. One may use warm, friendly details. Another may use bleak, empty ones.
draft.remember: A representation is a version of a person or place, built from the creator's choices and context.

a.q: What is a representation in a text?
opts: A version of a person or place built through choices
An exact copy of a person or place as it really is
A summary of the plot of a story or film
A list of facts about a person or place
a.why: A representation is a portrayal that the creator builds by choosing what to include and how to show it. It is not an exact copy of reality, because those choices always shape what the audience sees.
a.clue: Think about who decides what appears in the text.

b.q: A travel blog describes a seaside town with sunny photos, friendly locals and no mention of the empty shops. What does this show?
opts: The blogger chose details to portray the town positively
The blogger has shown the town exactly as it is
The town has no problems of any kind
The photos were taken by someone else
b.why: The blogger selected some details and left out others, which creates a positive representation. It does not prove the town is perfect, because leaving out the empty shops is also a choice.
b.clue: Notice what is included and what is left out.

a.best: A version of a person or place built through choices

b.best: The blogger chose details to portray the town positively
